case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread discusses the Bluetooth SIG registration process for multiple product models that share the same Bluetooth implementation. The customer asks whether different products with different use cases can have unique Product Names during listing. The consultant confirms the correct structure of using a single Design Name while allowing multiple Product Names under the Product List. The discussion also includes administrative steps such as payment of the qualification fee, required documentation, and handling of additional product registrations.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The main technical point is the distinction between Design Name and Product Name in the Bluetooth qualification database. A single Design represents the shared Bluetooth implementation, while multiple end products can be listed under it. The Product List allows each product entry to have a unique Product Name even if they share the same Design. The thread also touches on how derivative products can be added to the Product List without redefining the Design. Additionally, it clarifies documentation requirements for compliance and how listing expansion is handled procedurally.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The consultant's reasoning is based on the principle that the Bluetooth Design (i.e., the implementation of the Bluetooth stack and related functionality) is the unit of qualification, not the end product itself. As long as the Design is unchanged, multiple products can reuse it and be listed under the same Design Name. Product differentiation is handled at the Product List level, allowing unique Product Names without requiring new qualification work.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: If the customer misunderstands the Design vs Product structure, they may incorrectly create multiple Designs for identical implementations, leading to unnecessary qualification fees and duplicated effort. This could also increase administrative complexity and delay product listing. Additionally, failing to follow the correct listing structure could result in inconsistencies in the Bluetooth SIG database or require re-submission.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Always separate the concept of 'Design' (Bluetooth implementation) from 'Product' (end device). Reuse a single qualified Design for multiple products whenever the Bluetooth functionality is unchanged, and differentiate products only at the Product List level to minimize cost and effort.
